_note: The Last Signal. Adds to the sourced `events` in data/objects.json; it does not replace them. `launch` dates come from the NSSDCA record named in `source`. `signal` marks the last documented event. `match` is a phrase from that object's event label, and `documented` says whether our sources record an actual final communication (true) or only the last documented event (false). Nothing here is a quoted transmission or log. See docs/research-sources.md (The Last Signal).

signal.title: Stopped working after lunar sunset
signal.note: The record gives the day it stopped working after its first lunar sunset. It does not describe a final transmission.

signal.title: Left behind as a launch pad
signal.note: Our sources describe no communication from the descent stage after the ascent stage lifted off. Its last documented event is serving as the launch pad.

signal.title: No last signal: still in use
signal.note: It is a passive mirror and needs no power. It never transmits: observatories bounce laser light off it, and that work continues.

signal.title: Stopped accepting commands from Earth
signal.note: NASA's record gives the date it stopped accepting commands, which ended the experiment.

signal.title: Parked after the final moonwalk
signal.note: Our sources do not record when the rover's equipment last communicated with Earth. The last documented event is the crew's final moonwalk before they left.

signal.title: Switched off from Earth
signal.note: It did not fall silent by itself: it was shut down on 30 September 1977, together with all the other Apollo science stations.

signal.title: Contact lost
signal.note: NASA's record gives the date contact was lost.

signal.title: Communications lost
signal.note: The lander and rover worked until 27 September 1997, when communications were lost. The reason is not known.

signal.title: Last transmission
signal.note: Stuck in soft sand, its solar panels could not gather enough sunlight to survive the winter.

signal.title: Last message to Earth
signal.note: NASA's catalogue: the final communication from the rover was received on 10 June 2018, during a planet-wide dust storm.

signal.title: Last signal
signal.note: As the Martian summer ended, its solar panels got less sunlight.

signal.title: Last contact with Earth
signal.note: After it missed two more calls, NASA declared the mission over on 21 December 2022.
